We need solve this SWE-bench task. Modify the repository to fix the issue, then leave the working tree with the patch applied.

Set disabled prop on ReadOnlyPasswordHashField
Description

Currently the django.contrib.auth.forms.UserChangeForm defines a clean_password method that returns the initial password value to prevent (accidental) changes to the password value. It is also documented that custom forms for the User model need to define this method: ​https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.1/topics/auth/customizing/#a-full-example
A while ago the forms.Field base class gained the ​disabled argument to:
[disable] a form field using the disabled HTML attribute so that it won’t be editable by users. Even if a user tampers with the field’s value submitted to the server, it will be ignored in favor of the value from the form’s initial data.
It seems to me that this property could be set to True be default on the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField used to display the password hash. This way the clean_password is no longer necessary and the potential pitfall when using the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField without implementing clean_password is removed.

I've modified the `ReadOnlyPasswordHashField` class in `django/contrib/auth/forms.py` to set the `disabled` property to `True` by default.

The change adds `kwargs.setdefault("disabled", True)` to the `__init__` method, which ensures that the field is disabled by default. This means the field will not be editable by users, and any submitted value will be ignored in favor of the initial data, which is exactly the behavior we want for a read-only password hash field.

This change eliminates the need for custom forms to implement a `clean_password` method to prevent accidental password changes, as the disabled field will automatically ignore any submitted values. This makes the API safer by default and reduces the potential for security issues in custom user forms.

The working tree now contains this patch, which addresses the issue by leveraging Django's built-in `disabled` field property to properly handle read-only password display.
